change: The Web viewer treats selection of the same publication generation and media elements as a no-op, retains the shared player/audio output across supported rebinds, and rejects callbacks for a stale selection. A current remote publication with no first frame gets one video-only automatic retry after the 5-second observation deadline; a current SDK subscription failure can trigger that retry immediately before the first frame. The deadline pauses while the document or stage is hidden and while the sender pauses video. Automatic recovery is suppressed for an ended/local/muted/non-visible/autoplay-blocked selection and after its one attempt; a failure after the first frame remains available for manual retry. Current TrackSubscribed clears only the matching selected failure. If a publication disappears or is replaced without proven session identity, the viewer ends the selection and requires an explicit new choice.

limitation: The current Web LiveKit adapter does not carry the shared v1 session descriptor. Same-generation recovery is therefore bounded to the still-present SDK publication object; disappearance or replacement fails closed. Local tests do not prove audible output, actual first-frame latency, browser stage visibility/background suspension, SFU recovery, device compatibility, autoplay behavior or long-run memory stability. No SDK keyframe/PLI API was introduced.
